svg.title: Before and after the yellow line
svg.desc: Small multiples in five columns: evacuation orders, white phosphorus attacks, fires, and detonations and demolitions, before the yellow line was announced (1 March to 12 April 2026) and after it (20 April to 14 October 2026), each category on its own scale shared by both rows; and the glyphosate spraying of 1 February 2026, before the window, drawn once in the top row as the 10 border communities whose agricultural land CNRS-L lists as affected (2,122 ha), each circle in proportion to its hectares, with its bottom panel empty.
svg.text: Before and after the yellow line was announced (18 April 2026)
Each category is counted apart and drawn on its own scale, the same in both rows; rates are per week of the period. The glyphosate spraying was
one operation, before the window: it has no rate, and its communities are drawn once, sized by hectares of agricultural land.
The published counts are weekly and the yellow line was announced on a Saturday, so the week of 13 to 19 April 2026 is drawn in neither row: 2 orders, 2
white phosphorus attacks, 7 fires and 13 detonations and demolitions.
Evacuation orders not shaded: those naming no town (31 before, 3 after), a place with no mapped point (19 before, 7 after) or a town beyond the frame (14
Glyphosate spraying, from the CNRS-L report of 22 May 2026: the ten communities of its table of affected agricultural land (2,122 ha as printed), each circle on
the community's gazetteer point, as on this report's glyphosate map, which places the village and not the land affected. Borj an-Naqoura is drawn at
An-Naqoura; Btayshiyeh, which has no gazetteer point, inside its approximate territory; and the table's Al-Marwaniyeh (401 ha) at Marwahin, since a town of
that name lies in Sidon district, 39 km to the north, and the report's own map of the sampling sites names Marwahin in this strip. Sampling sites at the
coordinates the report prints, read as UTM zone 36N; the army's samples 774 and 777 have no usable position and are not drawn.
